title: Redwood All-Hands - January 2026 - Leadership Update
summary: Monthly company all-hands: CEO update on business and strategy, product leadership on roadmap and performance, engineering on infra and Dedicated/Private progress, people/hiring update, and Q&A. Recorded with some minor transcription artifacts.
topics: Q1 roadmap priorities: reliability, cost optimization, private deployments
transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um I know it's a busy week so appreciate you carving time in, we'll run about an hour, lots to get through. Quick housekeep, slides are in the #all-hands channel, recording will be posted.
[00:31] Ava: Quick snapshot: we closed December at 6.8M ARR, that's +24% quarter over quarter, which is ahead of plan. A lot of that is from a few larger Dedicated deals and some expansion from existing hosted customers, so nice work sales and SEs.
[01:05] Samir: Yeah team - shout out to the SEs who ran benchmarks with the Acme and NeoHealth pilots, that helped accelerate procurement. There were a couple of procurement delays but we got them over the line.
[01:42] Ava: On margin we still have work to do, token-level costs are down 8% year on year but we need another 10-12% to hit Q2 targets. That means more batching and cache work plus a push on quantization profiles.
[02:15] Ravi: On infra, we shipped the continuous batching improvements late December. Early results show 12% lower p99 CPU usage on mixed workloads, though there's still some tail latency for long-prompt use cases. We're tracking a KV cache regression reported by an enterprise customer, it's "kay vee cache" in the notes sometimes spelled out, but the gist is a cache invalidation bug on long sessions. Root cause is identified, patch in staging today.
[02:50] Ethan: We'll be running an A/B rollout next week, canary 5% of traffic to the patched runtime and run the existing bench suite. If all green we promote. There could be slight perf variance on very short token streams, so we'll include the latency SLOs in the test.
[03:22] Maya: Product is prioritizing three Q1 bets: 1) Reliability hardening across hosted and dedicated, 2) Private beta for VPC/on-prem with improved KMS integrations, and 3) Optimize toolkit - smarter batching and quantization suggestions surfaced in Console.
[03:55] Audience (someone off-mic): any timeline on Private GA?
[04:05] Maya: We're targeting Private GA in late Q1 for a limited set of cloud partners; on-prem GA will be later, depends on customer pilots. Also compliance work (SOC2/ISO) is on track to finish a couple of attestations this quarter.
[04:40] Janelle: On hiring, we hit the bar for IC hiring in infra and product — hiring plan posted, expect 18 net hires in Q1 focused on runtime, SEs, and security. There will be a tighter bar for managers; we want to keep org lean.
[05:10] Samir: We'll also be expanding the solutions engineering roster to support Dedicated ramp — customers ask for throughput guarantees and on-site bench help.
[05:36] Ava: Quick customer highlights: NeoHealth pilot for private inference passed HIPAA checklist and is moving to a 6 month POC; FinEdge signed a Dedicated contract for 12 months; another notable win was Workshop AI choosing us for cost predictability reasons.
[06:05] Audience Q&A starts: 
[06:20] Employee 1: Can we get more details on the pricing changes mentioned?
[06:28] Samir: We'll share a pricing FAQ, the core change is clearer unit economics for embeddings vs. generation plus committed discounts for Dedicated. No immediate change to hosted per-token pricing for existing customers; new customers will see simplified tiers.
[07:05] Employee 2: What's the rollback plan if the KV cache patch creates regressions?
[07:14] Ethan: Immediate rollback to previous runtime binary is in our runbook, and we have auto-fallback policies at the routing layer so customers can fall back to compatible model variants. We'll also do an emergency canary if needed.
[07:40] Ava: On the strategic front, our thesis is about serving — making inference predictable and cheap for customers. We'll continue to invest in both foundational infra and vertical integrations (healthcare, finance).
[08:05] Ravi: A quick tech highlight — we added a new kernel selection heuristic that chooses kernels based on sequence-length distribution. Early results show 6% latency improvement for medium-length prompts on A100-class hardware, it's incremental but important at scale.
[08:45] Audience (murmur):
[09:00] Maya: Console updates — per-route dashboards are live internally; we'll open them to beta customers next week. It surfaces token-level cost, latency percentiles, and a suggestions pane for batching and quantization. Expect a deck.
[09:30] Ava: Security: our SOC2 Type II engagement is underway; auditors asked for additional sampling on customer logs retention. We're working with Legal and Infra to provide the artifacts.
[10:00] Janelle: For managers - please review the updated PTO policy and return-to-office guidelines in #people. We'll do small team office days starting Feb.
[10:20] Q&A continues with cross-talk and short interruptions, some mics popping so the transcript has a few omissions.
[15:05] Maya: On Dedicated: ops have reduced the cold-start for large models from ~18s to ~12s with instance pre-warm heuristics; still working on further reduction especially across multi-tenant pools.
[16:00] Ravi: We're also enabling hardware-aware routing — if latency SLO is strict we'll route to lower-utilization Dedicated nodes, else to lower-cost pooled capacity. This will be in the routing config and Console soon.
[18:20] Samir: From sales cadence perspective, please highlight three case studies in customer outreach: FinEdge (finance), NeoHealth (healthcare), and Workshop AI (SaaS). Templates will be in the GTM drive.
[21:10] Employee 3 (ask): Any changes to stock refreshers or compensation?
[21:25] Ava: We'll publish an update to total comp guidelines after the board meeting next month; no immediate changes this quarter.
[22:00] Audience: applause and a few quick shoutouts to new hires.
[25:00] Ethan: Technical deep dive invite — if you're interested in how kernel selection works or want to see the bench results, join the infra deep dive next Wed; sign-up link in the invite.
[28:10] Maya: Roadmap ask - product will ship a public roadmap page by end of Jan that shows major themes and not detailed dates.
[30:00] Ravi: Note on incident postmortems - we're changing the format to include SLO impact in the first section, and an action-tracking table. Postmortems will be linked from Console incidents.
[35:10] Janelle: People update - reminder about new interview kits and inclusive hiring training. Also parental leave policy clarifications posted.
[40:00] Open floor - short employee highlights, kudos. A few folks mention cross-team blockers; leadership asked teams to use the weekly syncs to escalate.
[47:20] Ava: Final remarks - focus for Q1: (1) reliability to meet enterprise SLOs, (2) private deployments for regulated customers, and (3) tooling to cut token costs. If we hit those, we set up Q2 for scale.
[48:10] Audience: several questions about timelines, some follow-ups noted.
[50:00] Closing recap: Ava: I'll send the slide deck, roadmap link, and hiring plan. Managers: please review hiring queues and interviewing panels. SEs: prioritize upcoming bench requests.
[51:00] Meeting ends; recording stops. Transcription quality medium—some words garbled (e.g., "kay vee cache", occasional speaker label swaps), typical of large all-hands recordings.
